gettingAround.rentalCars: Essential for exploring properly. Book in advance for summer — prices triple in July/August. Faro airport has all major companies. Avoid the cheapest options (hidden fees); mid-range is best value.
gettingAround.publicTransport: EVA buses connect main towns but are slow and infrequent. The train runs Faro-Lagos along the coast — scenic but limited stops. Without a car, you'll miss the best beaches and restaurants.
gettingAround.taxis: Uber works in larger towns (Faro, Albufeira, Lagos, Portimão). Traditional taxis are metered but can be expensive. Agree on price for longer trips. Apps: Uber, Bolt, Free Now.
gettingAround.parking: Free parking is disappearing fast. Most beach car parks are now paid (€1-3/hour, or €5-10/day). Bring coins. Blue lines = paid; white lines = free; yellow lines = no parking.
tips: The A22 motorway is now toll-free — use it for long distances, saves 30-45 minutes Faro to Lagos
GPS sometimes directs you through tiny village roads — trust main routes for long drives
Roundabouts are everywhere — the car already in the roundabout has right of way

dining.couvert: When you sit down, bread, butter, olives, and sometimes cheese or pâté will appear on your table. This is the 'couvert' and it is NOT free — typically €1-5 per person. You can send it back (politely say 'não, obrigado') if you don't want to pay for it. This is the #1 surprise for first-time visitors.
dining.mealTimes: Lunch is 12:30-2:30pm, dinner 7:30-10pm. Arriving at 6pm for dinner will get you an empty restaurant and confused staff. Portuguese eat late — 8:30pm is standard for dinner.
dining.portions: Portuguese portions are generous. 'Dose' is a full portion (usually feeds 2), 'meia dose' is a half portion (feeds 1). Many restaurants let you order meia dose — always ask. Petiscos (small plates) are meant to share.
dining.waterAndWine: Tap water is safe and free — ask for 'água da torneira.' House wine (vinho da casa) is almost always good and cheap (€5-10 a jug). Don't pay for fancy bottled water unless you want to.

money.currency: Euro (€). Portugal is part of the Eurozone.
money.tipping: Not obligatory but appreciated. Round up or leave 5-10% for good service at restaurants. Coffee/bar: round up to nearest euro. Taxis: round up. Hotels: €1-2 per bag for porters.
money.cashVsCard: Cards accepted almost everywhere, but small tascas and markets often prefer cash. Always carry €30-50 in small bills. Contactless widely available.
money.atms: Multibanco ATMs are everywhere and reliable. They have the best exchange rates. Avoid airport exchange bureaus (terrible rates). Your bank may charge fees — check before travel.

apps.name: Google Maps
apps.tip: Download offline maps for the Algarve before you go. Cell service can be spotty in the interior and on beaches.

apps.name: Uber / Bolt
apps.tip: Both work in Faro, Albufeira, Lagos, Portimão. Bolt is often slightly cheaper. Neither works well in small towns.

apps.name: Windy
apps.tip: Essential for beach planning. Check wind direction — west coast gets Atlantic wind that makes some days cold. Surf forecasts included.

apps.name: GetYourGuide / Viator
apps.tip: Book cave tours and popular activities 2-3 days ahead in summer. Read recent reviews — quality varies.

apps.name: TheFork
apps.tip: The go-to app for booking restaurants in Portugal. Shows real-time availability, often has discounts (up to 50% off), and reviews are from actual diners. Much more reliable than Google reviews for Portuguese restaurants.

emergency.pharmacies: Look for green cross sign. Farmácias are everywhere and well-stocked. Pharmacists can advise on minor issues. 24-hour pharmacies rotate — check door signs for nearest night pharmacy (farmácia de serviço).
